**Flow: issue-10 (greet `--format json|text` flag) — implementation verified, merged, and re-checked on main. Nothing in flight; one proposed next step below.**

## Final report

**What broke:** nothing was broken per se — the `greet` command simply lacked the required `--format` capability, and the test suite covered only the text path.

**What changed:** PR #11 (branch `issue-10/implementation`) merged to main as `8ab5e4f`. It adds `--format` with `choices=["text","json"]`, default `text` (existing behavior untouched), a `format_greeting()` helper that wraps the message via `json.dumps({"message": ...})` for json, and three new tests — default format, explicit text, and json (parsed and asserted on the `message` key). Verification before merge: I read the full diff against issue #10's acceptance criteria. Re-check after merge, on a fresh clone of updated main: `python3 -m pytest test_fixture_feature.py` → **4 passed**, and a live CLI invocation `greet Ada --format json` printed exactly `{"message": "Hello, Ada!"}`.

**What became possible:** the CLI now emits machine-parseable output, so scripts can consume `greet` results as JSON, and both formats are pinned by tests against regression.

**What limits remain:** the repo has no CI, so "checks passed" rests on my local run rather than a pipeline; `--format` only affects `greet` (help output/other future subcommands aren't formatted); and the board under `docs/issue-10/` has no records yet.

## Proposed next role

The board shows an executable artifact landed on main with no execution-observation record for commit `8ab5e4f` — that's exactly `execution-observation`'s board condition (observe real runtime behavior, no fixing). That's my recommendation for the next spawn; say the word and I'll launch it. Alternatively, if you consider the fixture scenario complete, issue #10 can be closed as delivered (PR #11 carried `Closes #10`, so GitHub likely closed it on merge already).
